tagline: From the St. Lawrence up the Black River valley toward Rome.
intro: The road mapped here starts at Ogdensburg on the St. Lawrence and runs south through Gouverneur, Harrisville and Croghan to Lowville. The Adirondack regional guide's 111-mile trail also takes in Ogdensburg, Croghan and Lowville. NYSDOT's own page describes a different line, 94 miles from Rome down the river to Dexter and Black River Bay on Lake Ontario.

From Lowville the road follows the Black River valley upstream, with the Tug Hill Plateau to the west and the Adirondacks to the east, past Lyons Falls and Boonville and on to Rome. The middle forty miles of the river have practically no fall, and it holds trout, salmon, bass and pike.

moments.title: Ogdensburg
moments.text: The city sits where the Oswegatchie River meets the St. Lawrence, and its port is the only American one on the St. Lawrence Seaway.

moments.title: Lowville
moments.text: The county seat is named for an early landowner, Nicholas Low, and has nothing to do with low ground or the lowing cattle of the dairy farms around it.

moments.title: Lyons Falls
moments.text: The Moose River comes in from the east just above the village, and then the Black River drops 70 feet over a gneiss cliff.
